newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to revamp media control law - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to revamp media control law - paper.

text.p: Restrictions on the amount of the media that big proprietors can control will be scrapped and ownership regulated instead by general competition laws under a plan which is gathering strong government support, the Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Monday.

"It has the backing of the Minister for Communictions and the Arts, Senator (Richard) Alston, who believes fixed share limits like the existing cross-media laws, are too inflexible and difficult to administer," the newspaper said.

"The plan is likely to be the model recommended by the government's review of media laws," it said. "It is also the one most favoured by the major media players which have backed it in their submissions to the review."

The newspaper said the government would change existing competition laws to allow the anti-monopolies watchdog, The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), to block deals which would seriously reduce ownership diversity.
Under current cross-media regulations, which are currently subject to a government review, media proprietors are not allowed to control both broadcast and print media in the same market.
The laws, for example, currently prevent media mogul Kerry Packer from fulfilling his wish to take control of the John Fairfax Holdings Ltd newspaper group.
Packer also controls the Nine Network television business through his control of Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
Canadian Conrad Black now effectively controls Fairfax with a 25 percent stake and has said he wants to move to at least 50 percent equity.

Alston said the issue of foreign ownership would not be addressed by the current review. However, he added: "I think it's fair to say that in due course, we will have to contemplate an ongoing approach to foreign ownership."
